summary: routers/invoices.py implements all 4 endpoints per the task plan and DS-023: list (any-auth), create-from-sales (SUPERVISOR, sales_header_id as Query param), get detail (any-auth), record-payment (SUPERVISOR). InvoiceService is wired via Depends(get_invoice_service). AC-069/TC-217 shape is fully supported.

spec.notes: 4 routes match plan; response_model, status_code, and auth gates match. sales_header_id is Query(...) per plan/DS-023. Signatures line up with InvoiceService methods list_invoices/create_from_sales/get_invoice/record_payment (record_payment receives the full PaymentCreate payload, matching the actual service signature — the plan's snippet showed payload.amount but the service expects PaymentCreate, so the implementation correctly reconciles this).

contract.notes: Imports resolve: InvoiceService (T-084), get_current_user + require_supervisor + get_invoice_service (T-089 dependencies.py), InvoiceRead/InvoiceSummary/PaymentCreate (T-082 schemas/pricing.py), UserModel (T-076 models/auth.py). No unused imports. router.prefix='/invoices' and tags=['invoices'] match expected mount in main.py.

test.notes: TC-217 (integration): POST /invoices?sales_header_id=5 with SUPERVISOR JWT. Router returns 201 with InvoiceRead as required. invoice_number/total_amount/status/lines are produced by InvoiceService.create_from_sales — router path is a pure delegation. 404 (sales not found) and 409 (already invoiced) exceptions raised by the service propagate directly.

security.notes: Auth enforced: GET endpoints require Depends(get_current_user); POST endpoints require Depends(require_supervisor) per DS-019. sales_header_id typed as int (FastAPI validation). status Query filter is regex-restricted to ^(PENDING|PARTIAL|PAID)$. PaymentCreate.amount validated gt=0 at schema level (T-082). No secrets exposed. No user-controlled string interpolation into SQL — all DB access flows through the service/repository layer.

structural.notes: graphify-out/graph.json not consulted (structural lens optional; router will be reachable from main.py via include_router per T-093).

findings.description: The list_invoices query-param `status: str | None = Query(...)` shadows the imported `fastapi.status` module inside the function scope. There is no runtime bug — the `@router.post(..., status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)` decorators are evaluated at module load before the parameter exists, and the function body does not reference the status module. However, the shadowing is a mild readability trap for future editors who may add `raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, ...)` inside list_invoices and be surprised.
findings.fix_instruction: Optional: rename the parameter to `status_filter` (matching the InvoiceService kwarg it forwards to) or import `from fastapi import status as http_status`. Leaving as-is is acceptable since the function body does not use the status module.

findings.description: The LLD entry for routers/invoices.py describes create_invoice's sales_header_id as `int (JSON body)`, but the task plan explicitly overrides this with `Query(...)` per DS-023 (on-demand pattern), and TC-217 in test_cases.json also shows the request body containing sales_header_id. The implementation follows the plan (Query param). This is a documented plan override, not an implementation defect — flagging so the audit trail records the LLD-vs-plan reconciliation. The test harness for TC-217 will need to submit sales_header_id as a query string, not a JSON body, to match the router.
findings.fix_instruction: No code fix. Recommend the sprint-close/final-audit note the LLD text drift so a future LLD refresh can align the `(JSON body)` annotation with the implemented Query semantics.
